claims.quote: Here, we identified cyclin-dependent kinase-like 5 (CDKL5), known to function in neurodevelopment, as an essential regulator of virophagy.
Loss-of-function mutations in CDKL5 are associated with a severe neurodevelopmental encephalopathy.
Loss-of-function mutations in CDKL5 are associated with a severe neurodevelopmental encephalopathy.
Mechanistic studies demonstrated that CDKL5 directly binds the canonical selective autophagy receptor p62 and phosphorylates p62 at T269/S272 to promote its interaction with viral capsid aggregates.
